description: Somo hili linafundisha aina za vitenzi, nyakati (uliopita, uliopo na ujao), hali za vitenzi, minyambuliko ya vitenzi, pamoja na viambishi vya nafsi na wakati.

mcq.questionText: Katika sentensi 'Juma alisoma kitabu jana', kiambishi cha wakati ni kipi?
mcq.explanation: The infix '-li-' marks the past tense (wakati uliopita), as in 'alisoma' (he/she read).

mcq.questionText: Kiambishi '-na-' katika kitenzi 'anacheza' kinaonyesha wakati gani?
mcq.explanation: The infix '-na-' marks the present tense (wakati uliopo), so 'anacheza' means 'he/she is playing'.

mcq.questionText: Ni kiambishi kipi kinachoonyesha wakati ujao?
mcq.explanation: The infix '-ta-' marks the future tense (wakati ujao), as in 'atakuja' (he/she will come).

mcq.questionText: Katika kitenzi 'tunaimba', kiambishi 'tu-' kinawakilisha nafsi gani?
mcq.explanation: The subject prefix 'tu-' represents the first person plural (we), as in 'tunaimba' (we are singing).

mcq.questionText: Neno gani kati ya yafuatayo ni kitenzi?
mcq.explanation: 'Kuandika' (to write) is a verb in its infinitive form; a verb expresses an action or state.

mcq.questionText: Kitenzi 'kupika' kikinyambuliwa katika kauli ya kutendewa kinakuwa:
mcq.explanation: The applicative-passive (kutendewa) of 'pika' is 'pikiwa', meaning to have something cooked for one, e.g. 'alipikiwa chakula'.

mcq.questionText: Katika sentensi 'Mlango umefungwa', kiambishi '-me-' kinaonyesha hali gani?
mcq.explanation: The infix '-me-' marks the perfect aspect (hali timilifu), showing a completed action with present relevance, e.g. 'umefungwa' (it has been closed).

mcq.questionText: Kauli ya kutendeka ya kitenzi 'soma' ni ipi?
mcq.explanation: The stative form (kutendeka) of 'soma' is 'someka', showing the possibility or state of being readable, e.g. 'kitabu kinasomeka'.

mcq.questionText: Sentensi 'Yeye hula wali kila siku' inaonyesha hali gani?
mcq.explanation: The prefix 'hu-' in 'hula' marks the habitual aspect (hali ya mazoea), used for actions done regularly, e.g. 'hula' (usually eats).

mcq.questionText: Kauli ya kutendesha (kusababisha) ya kitenzi 'lala' ni ipi?
mcq.explanation: The causative (kutendesha) of 'lala' is 'laza', meaning to make someone sleep, e.g. 'mama alimlaza mtoto'.
The prefix 'si-' is the first person singular negative marker (ukanushi); 'sitakwenda' means 'I will not go'.

mcq.questionText: Kitenzi kishirikishi (copula) kipo katika sentensi gani?
mcq.explanation: 'Ni' in 'Baba ni mkulima' is a copula verb (kitenzi kishirikishi) that links the subject to its description.

mcq.questionText: Kauli ya kutendwa (passive) ya kitenzi 'andika' ni ipi?
mcq.explanation: The passive (kutendwa) of 'andika' is 'andikwa', e.g. 'barua iliandikwa' (the letter was written).

mcq.questionText: Katika sentensi 'Nikipata pesa nitanunua baiskeli', kiambishi '-ki-' kinaonyesha nini?
mcq.explanation: The infix '-ki-' marks the conditional aspect (hali ya masharti), meaning 'if/when', e.g. 'nikipata' (if I get).
The root (mzizi) of the verb is '-chek-' (from 'cheka', to laugh); the other parts are affixes for subject, tense and object.

fib.explanation: The infix '-li-' marks the past tense, e.g. 'alisoma'.
The infix '-ta-' marks the future tense, e.g. 'atasoma'.

fib.questionText: Katika kitenzi 'ninakula', kiambishi cha nafsi ni _____.
fib.explanation: The prefix 'ni-' is the first person singular subject marker (I).

fib.questionText: Kauli ya kutendwa (passive) ya kitenzi 'penda' ni _____.
fib.explanation: The passive form of 'penda' (to love) is 'pendwa' (to be loved).
The infix '-me-' marks the perfect aspect, e.g. 'amefika' (has arrived).

fib.questionText: Kauli ya kutendea (applicative) ya kitenzi 'lima' ni _____.
fib.explanation: The applicative form of 'lima' (to cultivate) is 'limia', e.g. 'alinilimia shamba'.

fib.questionText: Katika sentensi 'Wao watacheza', kiambishi cha nafsi ya tatu wingi ni _____.
fib.explanation: The prefix 'wa-' is the third person plural subject marker (they).

fib.questionText: Kauli ya kutendeka (stative) ya kitenzi 'vunja' ni _____.
fib.explanation: The stative form of 'vunja' (to break) is 'vunjika' (to get broken), e.g. 'kikombe kimevunjika'.

fib.questionText: Kiambishi cha mazoea kinachowekwa mwanzoni mwa kitenzi ni _____.
fib.explanation: The prefix 'hu-' marks the habitual aspect, e.g. 'husoma' (usually reads).

fib.questionText: Kauli ya kutendesha (causative) ya kitenzi 'soma' ni _____.
fib.explanation: The causative form of 'soma' (to read) is 'somesha' (to teach/make read), e.g. 'mwalimu hutusomesha'.

tf.explanation: The infix '-na-' correctly marks the present tense, e.g. 'anasoma'.

tf.questionText: Kitenzi ni neno linaloeleza tendo au hali.
tf.explanation: A verb (kitenzi) is a word that expresses an action or a state.
The infix '-ta-' marks the future tense, not the past; the past is '-li-'.

tf.questionText: Katika kitenzi 'unakula', kiambishi 'u-' kinawakilisha nafsi ya pili umoja.
tf.explanation: The prefix 'u-' is the second person singular subject marker (you).

tf.questionText: Kauli ya kutendwa ya kitenzi 'soma' ni 'somwa'.
tf.explanation: The passive (kutendwa) of 'soma' is 'somwa' (to be read), e.g. 'kitabu kinasomwa'.

tf.questionText: Kiambishi '-me-' kinaonyesha hali timilifu ya tendo lililokamilika.
tf.explanation: The infix '-me-' marks the perfect aspect showing a completed action, e.g. 'amemaliza'.

tf.questionText: Kauli ya kutendeka ya kitenzi 'pata' ni 'patikana'.
tf.explanation: The stative form of 'pata' (to get) is 'patikana' (to be available/obtainable).

tf.questionText: Kiambishi 'hu-' cha mazoea hakichukui kiambishi cha nafsi mbele yake.
tf.explanation: The habitual marker 'hu-' replaces the subject prefix, so we say 'husoma' for all persons, not 'ahusoma'.
'Haraka' is an adverb (kielezi), not a verb; it describes how an action is done.

tf.questionText: Kauli ya kutendea (applicative) huonyesha tendo linalofanyiwa mtu au kitu fulani.
tf.explanation: The applicative form (kutendea) shows an action done for or to someone/something, e.g. 'andikia' (write for/to).

summary.correctAnswer: Ni neno linaloonyesha tendo au hali fulani.
summary.explanation: A verb is a word expressing an action or state, e.g. 'kula', 'lala'.

summary.questionText: Nyakati kuu tatu za vitenzi vya Kiswahili ni zipi?
summary.correctAnswer: Wakati uliopita, wakati uliopo na wakati ujao.
summary.explanation: Kiswahili verbs mark three main tenses: past, present and future.

summary.questionText: Kiambishi cha wakati uliopo ni kipi?
summary.explanation: The present tense infix is '-na-', e.g. 'anaimba'.

summary.questionText: Kiambishi cha wakati uliopita ni kipi?
summary.explanation: The past tense infix is '-li-', e.g. 'aliimba'.

summary.questionText: Kiambishi cha wakati ujao ni kipi?
summary.explanation: The future tense infix is '-ta-', e.g. 'ataimba'.

summary.questionText: Hali timilifu inaonyeshwa na kiambishi gani?
summary.explanation: The perfect aspect uses '-me-' to show a completed action, e.g. 'amefika'.
The habitual aspect is shown by the prefix 'hu-', e.g. 'husoma', for actions done regularly.

summary.correctAnswer: Ni mabadiliko ya kitenzi ili kuunda kauli mbalimbali kama kutendwa, kutendea na kutendeka.
summary.explanation: Verb extensions change a verb's form to create different voices/derivations such as passive, applicative and stative.

summary.correctAnswer: Ni ni-, u-, a- (umoja) na tu-, m-, wa- (wingi).
summary.explanation: Subject prefixes are ni-, u-, a- in the singular and tu-, m-, wa- in the plural.

summary.questionText: Kauli ya kutendwa ina maana gani?
summary.correctAnswer: Ni hali ambapo mtenda hutendewa, mfano 'pendwa', 'andikwa'.
summary.explanation: The passive voice shows the subject receiving the action, formed with '-wa', e.g. 'pendwa'.

hoq.questionText: Katika sentensi 'Wanafunzi waliposoma kwa bidii, walifaulu mtihani', kiambishi '-po-' kinaleta maana gani?
hoq.explanation: The relative infix '-po-' here expresses time ('when'), linking the clause to the time the action happened, i.e. 'when they studied'.

hoq.questionText: Kitenzi 'fundisha' kimetokana na mnyambuliko gani wa kitenzi 'funza'?
hoq.explanation: 'Fundisha' (to teach) is the causative derivation, formed by adding '-isha' to cause someone to learn.

hoq.questionText: Ni sentensi ipi iliyotumia kauli ya kutendewa kwa usahihi?
hoq.explanation: 'Alipikiwa' is the applicative-passive (kutendewa): the child had porridge cooked for them, correctly showing a beneficiary of the action.
